svg.text: An interrupt, cycle by cycle: replace the DECODE instruction, trap, handle, return
programs/21_timer_interrupts.s on the cycle-exact model (performance build), cycles 830 to 853. Every cell is what the RTL does too (make test).
cycle 832: the timer interrupt is pending and enabled, so the instruction in DECODE does not go on: an interrupt pseudo-instruction takes its place.
cycle 833: in EXECUTE it traps like ecall: mepc = the replaced instruction, mcause = 2^63 + 7, MIE off, jump to mtvec; FETCH1..DECODE are flushed.
It never retires (MEMORY gets a bubble): an interrupt costs 4 cycles, the X term of cycles = N + 5 + L + 3F + R + K + I + D + X.
The handler moves MTIMECMP forward and runs mret, a flush back to mepc: the replaced instruction runs now, and the loop never notices.
Faded rows were fetched and then squashed; their slots are the bubbles the equation counts.
